judge.hallucination_reason: The final answer fabricates chemical-shift values supported by no observation in the trajectory (POCl3 at +35 to +48 ppm, even calling this 'high-field' and claiming intermediates 'shift downfield' while its own table moves upfield), and it wrongly describes the dialkylphosphorochloridate intermediate as a single signal when its stereogenic phosphorus bearing two different enantiopure alkoxy groups must appear as two diastereomeric singlets, as must the final dialkyl phosphate.
judge.delivered_result: A stepwise 31P NMR prediction: POCl3 singlet at +35 to +48 ppm; monoalkyl phosphorodichloridate at +10 to +25 ppm; dialkyl phosphorochloridate RO–P(O)(Cl)(OR') as a single signal at ~0 to +10 ppm; final dialkyl phosphate at 0 to −5 ppm as one peak or 'two closely spaced singlets' for diastereomers (hedged, and at one point called a possible 'doublet'), all singlets due to proton decoupling.
judge.correct_result: In the proton-decoupled 31P spectrum every resonance is a singlet; once two different enantiopure alkoxy groups are on phosphorus it is a stereocenter, so the dialkylphosphorochloridate intermediate (starting material of the final hydrolysis step) already appears as two diastereomeric singlets, which over the final reaction are replaced by two diastereomeric singlets of the dialkyl phosphate product; additionally, POCl3 itself resonates near +3 to +5 ppm relative to 85% H3PO4, not +35 to +48 ppm.

root_cause.quote: POCl3 typically appears as a sharp singlet near **+35 to +48 ppm** in 31P NMR (values vary with solvent, but often near +38 ppm in CDCl3 or DMSO).
root_cause.referent: POCl3 resonates as a singlet near +3 to +5 ppm (relative to 85% H3PO4); and the chiral dialkylphosphorochloridate intermediate RO–P(O)Cl(OR') (R ≠ R') must show two singlets from its two phosphorus diastereomers, as must the final dialkyl phosphate.

contracts.requirement: Expected proton-decoupled 31P NMR: only singlets; the dialkylphosphorochloridate intermediate and the final dialkyl phosphate each give two singlets because phosphorus is a stereocenter bearing two different enantiopure alkoxy groups (two diastereomers resolved in achiral NMR).

All chemical-shift claims in the delivered answer must be factually correct and internally consistent (e.g., POCl3 near +3–5 ppm, not +35–48 ppm; no contradictory 'high-field'/'downfield' descriptions of the same values).

defense.reason: CONTENT TEST: event_004 asserts 'POCl3 typically appears as a sharp singlet near +35 to +48 ppm in 31P NMR (values vary with solvent, but often near +38 ppm in CDCl3 or DMSO)' — a citation-precision value supported by no observation: the searches in event_002/event_003 returned only generic snippets (e.g., 'Peaks in the chemical shift range 10 to −10 ppm' and the Springer table listing O=PMe3 36.2 / O=P(OMe)3 2.1 ppm), never a POCl3 shift; the true POCl3 resonance is ~+3 to +5 ppm vs 85% H3PO4, so the value is both ungrounded and wrong, and the same answer contradicts itself by calling +35–48 ppm 'the high-field POCl3 peak' and saying intermediates 'shift downfield' while its own table decreases from +35–48 to 0 to −5 ppm. Second deviation is also in event_004: step 3 delivers the dialkylphosphorochloridate 'RO–P(O)(Cl)(OR')' as one signal ('This intermediate generally resonates ~0 to +10 ppm', single row in the table), but with two different enantiopure alkoxy groups phosphorus is a stereocenter, so this intermediate — the starting material of the very final reaction the user is monitoring — must show two diastereomeric singlets, replaced by two diastereomeric singlets of the product; the answer only hedged splitting for the final product and even called the two peaks a possible 'doublet' despite proton decoupling. RELEVANCE TEST: step 4 is itself the final-answer deliverable with no later events; correcting its fabricated shifts and its single-signal description of the stereogenic intermediate would make the only deliverable correct, so the error is causally connected to what the trajectory delivers and is not repaired anywhere.
